name: Altyn-Arashan
near: Ak-Suu (formerly Teplokluchenka), ≈10–12 km east of Karakol; from Ak-Suu to the springs it is ≈15 km up the gorge
elev: ≈2,435–2,600 m: trekking platforms (loc.wiki/AllTrails) give 2,350–2,435 m at the guesthouses, Too.kg and Visit Kyrgyzstan give 2,600 m at the springs; Nomad's Land gives 2,580 m. The “3,000 m” figure on some sites is overstated.
short: A high-mountain valley with radon and hydrogen sulfide hot springs (35–41 °C), a relict spruce forest and a view of the trapezoid of Palatka Peak (4,260 m). From Ak-Suu it is 15 km on foot (3–5 h) or 1.5–2.5 h by UAZ over one of the roughest roads in the Issyk-Kul region.
desc: Altyn-Arashan (“golden spring”) is the valley of the Arashan river above the village of Ak-Suu, a nature reserve (zakaznik) since 1963. At the confluence of the rivers stand a handful of guesthouses and yurt camps, each with its own bathhouse: radon water at 35 °C and hydrogen sulfide water at 41 °C year-round; there are also “wild” stone tubs by the river. The valley is dominated by Palatka Peak (the Aksuu Wall, 4,260 m). The road from Ak-Suu is 15 km of rocky climbing with fords: ordinary cars and rental cars are not allowed here, and the traffic is UAZ-469s/“bukhankas”, GAZ-66s and Nissan Patrols with local drivers; on foot it is 3–5 h with a gain of ≈600 m, and the trail is simple and obvious. This is where the classic trek over the Ala-Kul Pass (3,900 m) into the Karakol gorge starts or ends, and 5 km above the resort a side valley leads off toward the lake. Electricity comes from generators and solar, payment is cash only, and there is practically no mobile signal. At night, even in summer, it can drop to −2…−5 °C.
guide: Walk up and take a “bukhanka” down — that way you see the gorge and also get a dose of adventure on the rocks and fords that make rental companies forbid driving here. The bathhouses belong to different guesthouses: some have a wooden log cabin with 41 °C hydrogen sulfide water, others a free stone tub right by the river — walk around and choose. In the evening, when the day-tour tourists leave, the valley belongs to the few who stay overnight: watch Palatka Peak in the sunset light and the stars without city light pollution. Bring cash som and a warm sleeping bag: cards are not accepted, and it is cold at night even in July. If you plan Ala-Kul, don’t do it “in a day from the bathhouse”: the 3,900 m pass needs acclimatization and a separate day.
see: Hot bathhouses at the guesthouses (radon 35 °C, hydrogen sulfide 41 °C) and “wild” tubs by the river; Palatka Peak / the Aksuu Wall (4,260 m); a relict Tien Shan spruce forest; the upper Arashan valley and the side valley toward Ala-Kul; yurt camps; in winter — a snow-covered valley (access only by UAZ or on foot).
skip: If you have one day and a bad back, 2.5 h of jolting in a UAZ each way will not make you happy. If you expect a spa resort with infrastructure — here you get log cabins, generators and outdoor toilets. If you are traveling in a rental sedan — entering the gorge is usually forbidden by the rental contract.
diff: On foot: moderate — 15 km, gain ≈600 m, 3–5 h, the trail is obvious, safe for solo travelers. By vehicle: rough off-road for a prepared 4×4 with a local driver only. The Ala-Kul trek over the 3,900 m pass is hard and should be assessed separately.
when: June–September is the main season; October brings golden larches and fewer people (Backpack Adventures). In winter the valley is accessible (UAZ/on foot) and the bathhouses work, but there can be avalanches on the road (video, 2023). In May–June the fords may be higher than normal.
hours: The valley is open 24 hours; the bathhouses at the guesthouses operate by arrangement with the owners, usually until evening; there is no official schedule. Google Maps: 24 hours.
daytime: Leave Karakol in the morning (transfers start at 8:00–9:00); bathe in the evening after the day groups leave or early in the morning; if you stay overnight — the stars.
how: 1) Karakol → Ak-Suu: marshrutka (minibus) No. 350 from the market/center of Karakol (formerly ≈15 som, 2017; the current price is not confirmed), then 15 km on foot up the valley (3–5 h) or in a local UAZ. 2) A direct 4×4 transfer from Karakol (35 km, ≈2–2.5 h): Arashan Transfer, MYWAY, CBT Karakol, GetYourGuide. 3) On foot from the Ala-Kul Pass (the second part of the loop trek).
needcar: No, if you are ready to walk 15 km uphill; yes — only a prepared 4×4 (UAZ, GAZ-66, Patrol) with a local driver. An ordinary car or rental car — no.
self: Yes: on foot the trail is simple and safe for solo travelers (Backpack Adventures); book a place to stay in advance in season. For the Ala-Kul Pass you need experience and acclimatization; a guide is optional.
roadtype: From Karakol to Ak-Suu — paved road; then 15 km of rocky dirt road with steep sections, boulders and fords; according to reviews, vehicles have to be “jacked up” on the rocks; “rental companies forbid this road” (TripAdvisor 2024–2025). In winter avalanche debris is possible.
traveltime: Karakol → Ak-Suu 20–30 min; Ak-Suu → springs: on foot 3–5 h (15 km, gain ≈600 m), by UAZ 1.5–2.5 h; a direct transfer from Karakol is ≈2–2.5 h one way.
stay: Elsa guesthouse — 1,700 som/person with breakfast (2025 review) or 4,000 som for two with lunch and dinner (Oct. 2022, T—Zh); yurt camps ≈3,600 som/night with breakfast and dinner (TripAdvisor 2025); Eco Yurtcamp Arashan, Arashan Hotel (bathhouse free for guests, 2025); Ala-Kul Guesthouse Altyn-Arashan; a tent pitch — ≈100 som (2017). Visit Kyrgyzstan: simple guesthouses $10–15/night. A bed in a guesthouse 300 som + dinner 250 + breakfast 150 (2017, outdated).
net: There is practically no mobile signal in the valley (Too.kg: “no signal”; TripAdvisor: limited electricity and internet). According to NomadCar, a weak O!/MegaCom signal is possible near the cabins. Beeline strengthened its network in Karakol and the Ak-Suu District in 2026, but not in the gorge. Maps — offline, money — cash.
entry: Entry to the Arashan gorge is through a paid barrier of the Karakol forestry enterprise (Kaktus.media, 10.06.2025): per person — citizens of Kyrgyzstan 20 som, citizens of former USSR countries 100, foreigners 220 som; per vehicle — car 80, large vehicles 170, buses/trucks 300 som. Bathhouses: wild tubs by the river — free; a guesthouse bathhouse ≈250 som/person (Arashan Transfer, 2026) or 200–500 som (SaryTours 03.2026); a private cabin — ≈$12/person/h; for overnight guests it is often free. Karakol National Park from the Karakol gorge side — 300 som/person (2025).
transfer: From Karakol, 2026: MYWAY — Patrol 9,200 som, UAZ 13,200, GAZ-66 17,600 per vehicle (not final); Arashan Transfer — $85/seat (day tour), $55–85 shuttle, $290–360 private UAZ; GetYourGuide — $90/person; per 2024–2025 reviews — 5,000–11,000 som per jeep; SaryTours 03.2026 — 3,000–5,000 som one way in a local UAZ. Marshrutka No. 350 — pennies (15 som in 2017).
bring: Cash som (no cards), trekking shoes, a warm layer and a hat (down to −5 °C at night), a rain jacket, water/a filter (boil river water), swimwear and a towel, a snack, a power bank, a headlamp, an offline map, a sleeping bag if you camp.
warn: The road is extreme: 4×4 with a local driver only, and rental cars are not allowed here under the rental contract. The altitude is 2.4–2.6 km and nights are cold even in summer; the weather changes abruptly (snow in August happens). Boil river water. There is no signal — tell someone your route. In winter — avalanches on the road. The Ala-Kul Pass (3,900 m) is a separate hard day, not a “walk from the bathhouse”. Radon baths — 15–20 minutes at a time, there are medical contraindications. Since 2025 there has been a forestry barrier at the gorge entrance with an entry fee (foreigners 220 som/person + 80 for a car); demand a receipt.
food: Food is available only at guesthouses by arrangement: home-cooked dinners (lagman, plov, soup, flatbreads), breakfasts; 2017 guideline — dinner 250, breakfast 150 som, 2022 — half board included in 4,000 som for two. There is no café or shop in the valley — bring groceries and snacks from Karakol.
reviews: Google Maps: 4.8/5, 706 ratings (03.10.2026). TripAdvisor: 4.8/5, 219 reviews, No. 2 of 40 in Karakol, Travelers' Choice (07.10.2026). Pros: the scenery, the springs, the atmosphere, the hospitality. Cons: a very rough road, cold at night, weak electricity and signal, basic conditions.
p.sum: The best option is to walk up from Ak-Suu (15–16 km, +600–700 m, 3–5 h) and come down by UAZ, or to make Altyn-Arashan the finale of the loop Karakol gorge → Ala-Kul → Altyn-Arashan. You cannot bring your own or a rental sedan here: the 16 km of riverbed with boulders and two fords is passable only by local UAZs and GAZ-66s (Arashan Transfer from $55/seat, private UAZ from $290; MYWAY from 9,200 som for a Patrol). It is worth staying at least one night in a guesthouse with a bathhouse (≈$20–59), bringing cash and a warm sleeping bag.

p.iti.0.title: Day trip from Karakol
p.iti.0.plan: 08:00 transfer from Giraffe Coffee → 10:30 Altyn-Arashan, bathhouse, a walk up the valley → 17:30 descent → 19:00 Karakol. Or: marshrutka No. 350 at 07:30 to Ak-Suu, hike up 4–5 h, bathe and descend by UAZ.
p.iti.1.title: 2 days
p.iti.1.plan: Day 1: marshrutka to Ak-Suu, hike up 15 km, bathhouse, a night in a guesthouse. Day 2: out-and-back up the valley toward Palatka, descend on foot or by UAZ, in the evening — the Ak-Suu Kench springs.
p.iti.2.title: 4 days — the Ala-Kul loop
p.iti.2.plan: Karakol → national park (marshrutka No. 101, 30 som) → Sirota → Ala-Kul → pass → Altyn-Arashan → Ak-Suu (the reverse direction is also popular, but from the Altyn-Arashan side the climb to the pass is longer).
p.iti.3.title: What to combine it with
p.iti.3.plan: Karakol (cathedral, mosque) → Altyn-Arashan → Ala-Kul → Karakol gorge; the next day — Jeti-Oguz and Kok-Jaiyk along the southern shore.
p.season: June–September is the main season (July–August is crowded); late September–October — golden larches, down to −5 °C at night; winter — access by UAZ/on foot, bathhouses work, avalanches on the road; May–June — high fords. Snow in August is possible.
p.budget.economy: ≈4,000–6,000 som for 2 days: marshrutka 40×2, forestry fee 220, night + meals at a guesthouse ≈1,700–3,000, bathhouse 0–250, food for the road 500
p.budget.comfort: ≈15,000–25,000 som/person for 2 days: Arashan Transfer $85 or a private UAZ $290 per vehicle, guesthouse $59–91, horse $25
p.permits: No permit is needed. The Karakol forestry barrier at the gorge entrance (since 2025): foreigners 220 som, CIS citizens 100, Kyrgyz 20 som/person; car 80, large vehicles 170 som — demand a receipt. When trekking via Ala-Kul there is an additional Karakol National Park fee of 300 som/person at the suspension bridge.
p.access: With children — possible by UAZ, but the jolting lasts 2–2.5 h; on foot for teenagers. For older people — only by vehicle, mind the altitude of 2.5 km. With a stroller — no. With a dog — possible on foot (livestock and shepherd dogs).
